headline: Bank of Japan raises rates to highest level in 31 years and signals continuous cycle against inflation
summary: The Bank of Japan raised its benchmark rate to 1.25%, its highest level in 31 years. The decision signals a continuing tightening cycle aimed at containing inflation and preventing economic risks.
why: The Bank of Japan sets the policy rate for the world's fourth-largest economy. Its rate decisions shape yen funding costs, Japanese government bond yields and global carry-trade flows.
why_moved: The rate increase to 1.25% is the highest in 31 years and signals a continuing cycle against inflation, a shift that alters expectations for Japanese borrowing costs.
